title: Decoupled Canary Preservation and Automated Recovery
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds CanaryPreservationPolicy CRD and a background recovery runner to snapshot and rehydrate canary state (KV cache, shadow-captures, session-anchors). Improves rollback/recover time for staged rollouts; no customer-visible API changes by default.
description:
Summary: Introduce a decoupled "Canary Preservation" mechanism and an automated recovery pipeline to speed rollbacks and safe re-promotes for staged rollouts. Motivation: production canaries often require full traffic replay or expensive cache warm-ups when rollback/rollback-and-replay is needed. This PR adds a policy-driven preservation layer that snapshots minimal serving state (KV cache hints, sample shadow captures, session anchors) and an automated recovery job that can rehydrate that state onto a previous model instance, drastically reducing failover time and reducing corrective load on upstream systems.

Goals and non-goals: This PR focuses on(canary lifecycle and recovery) not model training, not full request replay, and not changing routing semantics. It is intended to be safe by default: preservation is opt-in via a CanaryPreservationPolicy and has TTL and SLO-budget constraints.

What changed (high-level): - New CRD CanaryPreservationPolicy to declare preservation windows and retention TTLs, cohort selectors, and SLO budget guards. - Controller: controller/canary_preserver.go implements snapshot creation, preservation lifecycle, and garbage collection. - Recovery runner: cmd/rdctl/recover.go and controller/recovery_runner.go add an operational path to rehydrate serving state and prime KV caches on an older model. - Runtime hooks: small additions to serving runtime to emit and accept preservation manifests and safe apply of preserved snapshots (runtime/preserver_hook.go). - Policy engine: pkg/policy/preservation_policy.go enforces SLO budget checks before automatic recovery. - Tests: integration-tests/preservation-recovery.test.ts and unit tests for TTL and GC behavior. - Docs & runbook: docs/runbooks/canary-preservation.md with playbook steps and escalation guidance.

Checklist: - [x] CRD schema and validation - [x] Controller + recovery-runner implementation - [x] Unit tests for policy guards and TTL GC - [x] Integration test demonstrating rollback+rehydrate reduces RPS spike - [x] Runbook & docs - [x] Backwards-compatible by default (preservation off unless policy present)

Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-8742/canary-preservation-design, incident reference SUP-1123 (related customer incident where replay costs spiked), runbook draft at docs/runbooks/canary-preservation.md

Additional notes: This PR intentionally keeps preserved payload sizes bounded (sampled captures and KV key-hints rather than full blob cache). Preservation manifests are stored in the control plane object store with retention TTL.

Commit summary and rationale (short):
- commit 1: add CRD CanaryPreservationPolicy, validation and API docs
- commit 2: controller scaffolding and snapshot lifecycle manager (create/persist/gc)
- commit 3: runtime hooks for export/import of minimal preservation manifests
- commit 4: recovery-runner CLI and controller integration (auto-recover mode behind feature flag)

review_conversation:
Evan Brooks: Could we quantify expected preservation storage per canary? Priya: Estimated ~50-200KB per cohort by default (sampled captures + key hints); added a config knob and metrics.
Maya Chen: Need an explicit SLO budget check before auto-recover; we don't want auto-recover to trigger during an active incident and consume extra capacity. Diego: added preservation_budget and dry-run mode; policy enforces remaining SLO budget > 10% by default.
Diego Alvarez: Unit test failing on GC race locally; suggested adding deterministic clock in tests. Priya: fixed by injecting test clock into GC loop, added determinism to unit tests.
Maya Chen: Please add a canary e2e showing 'rollback -> rehydrate -> stabilized' with RPS comparison. Priya: integration test added demonstrating ~70% reduction in spike compared to cold rollback.
Evan Brooks: Approve after documenting metrics and adding retention knob. Maya Chen: Approve. Diego Alvarez: Approve and requested a short follow-up to add a telemetry dashboard; follow-up ticket ENG-9405 opened.
ci_summary: Initial CI: tests/unit failed (GC race) on first run; author pushed fix and CI retried. Final CI: all checks passed. Checks: unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass on matrix small clusters), lint (pass), helm-lint (pass), e2e-smoke (pass).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash-merge into main on 2026-01-21 by Evan Brooks. Merge commit includes summarized CHANGELOG and a follow-up ticket link ENG-9405 for telemetry dashboard. Deployment notes: preserver feature behind feature flag 'preservation.enabled' set to false by default; customers must opt-in and create CanaryPreservationPolicy objects to enable.
